text: On Monday, Spaulding and Mister Wilson went to the address in Fleet Street, where they found the street full of red headed men. <break time="0.8s" /> Every shade of red was there, from orange to the color of bricks, but very few were as bright as his own hair. <break time="0.8s" /> Spaulding pushed and pulled until he had brought his master through the crowd and right up to the office. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside, a small man with even redder hair, Mister Duncan Ross, looked at Wilson and cried that he was perfect for the job. <break time="0.8s" /> Then he suddenly took hold of Wilsons hair with both hands and pulled until Wilson shouted with pain. <break time="0.8s" /> There are tears in your eyes, so I see that the hair is real, he said, but we have to be careful. <break time="0.8s" /> He explained that the work had to be done in the office from ten to two each day, and that Wilson must never leave the building. <break time="0.8s" /> If he left even once, he would lose the position forever, so Wilson promised to stay at his desk the whole time. <break time="0.8s" /> His task was to copy out the Encyclopaedia Britannica by hand, starting with the first volume under the letter A. <break time="0.8s" /> For eight weeks he wrote about Abbots, Archery, Armour, Architecture, and Attica, and every Saturday he received four golden sovereigns.
